$comment: Where each icon of sprites.txt comes from. A name absent here and present in maki is taken
from maki under its own name - that is the majority, and listing it would be noise.
'letter' is not artwork: the roundel's content IS a character, so the font map carries that
character and no glyph has to be drawn. The disc, its ring and the colours are the style's
(shield-icon-background-*), so only the content is sourced here.
'alias' takes another set's icon under a different name. 'approx' says the shape is a stand-in,
not the same drawing - it is listed so a reviewer can disagree with the choice.

external_door.approx: a doorway, not a building's outer door

inter_building_door.approx: a doorway, not a between-buildings one

cliff.approx: carries falling rocks, which maki's cliff does not

security.approx: a checkpoint stands in for a security post

$comment: Transit marks no open icon set carries, from Wikimedia Commons. `node fetch-commons.mjs`
downloads each into local/ under the SPRITE name. Every one of these is tagged Public
domain there - simple geometric shapes and text, below the threshold of originality - which
settles COPYRIGHT and not trademark: these are live marks of TfL, RATP/SNCF, MTA and the
rest. Labelling that network's own stations is the nominative use; anything else is not.
The files are the whole badge. Only the content belongs in a glyph, so each still has to be
stripped of its disc and its colours - except where the ring IS the mark (the roundels, the
National Rail double arrow), which keep it.
commons.new-york-subway: MTA New York City Subway logo.svg

letter.$comment: Content only - Massif draws the disc and the ring from the style's own colours.
